## First launch on Windows

Hamdori is a new app from a solo developer, and its Windows installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may show a warning and "Unknown publisher". The steps below are for the "Windows protected your PC" screen.

See the steps [...] See the steps

1. Open the Hamdori installer you downloaded.
2. When "Windows protected your PC" appears, click "More info".
3. The publisher shows as "Unknown publisher". If you downloaded the file from this site, click "Run anyway".
4. When setup finishes, Hamdori appears in the corner of your screen. Enter the key from your receipt.

On Windows 11 PCs with Smart App Control turned on, the installer may be blocked. You won't have activated your key yet, so you can get a refund. Download the installer only from this site.

## And while you work

### Take breaks together

Right-click the hamster, choose Break Together, then click the little clock. Focus for 25 minutes, then rest for 5 together.

@galdayanThanks for asking! On macOS I use CGEventSourceCounterForEventType(kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState, kCGEventKeyDown). It returns a count of key-down events, with no key codes, characters or app names. Hamdori checks it every 0.1 seconds, and when the count goes up, he nibbles.

The app never asks for Input Monitoring, and in my testing this call works without any permission prompt.

On Windows I use GetLastInputInfo, which only gives the time of the last input, not a key-press count.
